title: Scredington Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 9 killed (7 crew, 2 passengers) including pilot Plt Off. Max Keiran Cummings

external_narratives.summary: Detailed blog post about the Lancaster ED439 crash at Scredington. The aircraft dived out of cloud near Highgate Farm about 45 minutes after takeoff on 18 June 1943 and burnt on impact, killing all nine on board. The crew included an Australian pilot (PO Cummings RAAF), a Canadian rear gunner (FS Taylor RCAF), and two RAF Corporals believed to be wireless technicians.
key_details: Dived out of cloud 45 minutes after takeoff
Pilot PO Max Keiran Cummings was RAAF

memorial_details:
Stone of remembrance made of white marble, carved with pathfinder eagle at the top.

Memorial Display: The Avro Lancaster ED439 memorial displays the aircraft's details and history.
narrative: On 18 June 1943, Pilot Officer Cummings took off from RAF Wyton at the controls of Lancaster ED439, carrying seven crew members and two passengers on a daytime bombing target exercise. The aircraft, assigned to 83 Squadron's Pathfinder Force, failed to complete the training detail, diving through heavy cloud before crashing near Highgate Farm, Scredington, Lincolnshire. All nine on board were killed. Cummings was 30 years old and had served with the Royal Australian Air Force; his son, Peter Harrold Cummings, had been born just three months earlier, on 12 March 1943. The crew — T.J. Bond, Harry William Cheshire, H.W. Luker, John Roughley, Francis Neville Sloss, Robert Allan Taylor, Francis William Wilcox, and Norman Woodcock — are commemorated at a stone of remembrance at Scredington.
inscription:
ROYAL AIR FORCE
NO 83 (PATHFINDER) SQN
TO THE MEMORY OF THOSE
AIRMEN KILLED IN AIRCRAFT NO ED439 OL-N
CRASHED DURING A TRAINING FLIGHT
AT HIGHGATE FARM SCREDINGTON
18th JUNE 1943
[crew names inscribed on memorial]
LEST WE FORGET
